title: 2% Apartment Maintenance Fund: Who Pays and Who Manages It?
desc: Apartment 2% maintenance fund under the Housing Law 2023: based on apartment value, paid before handover, passed to the management board, common areas only.
summary: Who must pay the 2% maintenance fund for apartment buildings, where the money is held, when it is handed to the management board, and what it may be used for under the Housing Law 2023.
body: p

When buying an apartment from an investor, besides the sale price, the buyer must also pay the maintenance fund for the commonly owned parts. This sum often gives rise to disputes between residents and the investor. This article summarizes the rules in Articles 152–155 of the Housing Law 2023.
h2
1. Who must pay, and how much?
ul

Buyers and lease-purchasers of an apartment or other floor area from the investor pay 2% of the value of the apartment or floor area purchased. This amount is calculated separately from the purchase price and must be stated clearly in the contract (Clause 1, Article 152).

The investor that keeps apartments or floor areas it does not sell (except common parts) must also pay 2%, calculated on the highest apartment sale price in the building at the time of handover for use (Clause 2, Article 152).

For contracts signed before 1 July 2006 that did not collect a maintenance fund: the owners meet at an apartment building conference to agree on the contribution. For contracts signed from 1 July 2006 to before 1 August 2024 that did not agree on this sum, the investor must pay it (Clauses 3 and 4, Article 152).
h2
2. Where is the money paid?
p
Under Clause 1, Article 153:
ul

Before signing apartment sale contracts, the investor must open a separate account at a local credit institution to receive maintenance funds, and notify the provincial housing management authority within 5 working days.

The account number must be stated in the sale contract. The buyer pays before receiving the apartment; if they do not pay, the apartment is not handed over. If the investor hands over the apartment anyway, the investor must pay on the buyer's behalf.
The investor may not withdraw money from this account for other purposes before handing it over to the management board.
h2
3. When is it handed over to the management board?
ol
After the decision recognizing the apartment building management board, the board opens a separate account and sends a written request to the investor for handover.
Within 30 days, the two sides agree on the final reconciliation of the maintenance fund figures.
The bank transfers the entire fund together with interest to the account set up by the management board (Clause 2, Article 153).
p

While the fund has not yet been handed over, if a common item whose warranty has expired needs maintenance, the investor must pay from its own funds to carry it out first in accordance with the maintenance procedure, and is reimbursed upon handover if it has invoices and documents.
h2
4. What if the investor drags its feet and does not hand over?
p

The management board sends a written request to the authorities to require the investor to hand over. After 15 days the authorities must issue a written demand; if the investor still does not hand over after a further 10 days, the funds are forcibly recovered and given to the management board. If there are signs of a crime, the case is transferred to the investigating authority (Article 154 of the Housing Law). The enforcement sequence against each type of account, including seizure and auction of the investor's assets, is set out in Articles 87–91 of Decree 95/2024/ND-CP.
h2
5. What may the maintenance fund be used for?
ul
Only for maintaining and replacing items and equipment belonging to the commonly owned parts, under a maintenance plan approved by the apartment building conference (Clause 1, Article 155).

The management board may not use this fund for operating and management costs or any other purpose; every expense must have invoices and documents and be reported to the apartment building conference.
Once the 2% is used up, the owners continue to contribute when items need maintenance under the plan or on an unscheduled basis.
For a mixed-use building where the apartment area and commercial area can be separated, the fund is divided in proportion to the floor area of each area.
p

The 2% maintenance fund is different from the monthly operation and management fee. Buyers should also check the maintenance account details stated in the contract; see also Buying a home to be built in the future 2026.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The Housing Law 2023 and Decree 95/2024/ND-CP are partially no longer in force; Article 154 of the Housing Law still names "district-level People's Committee" as the authority under the former government model. When enforcement of handover is needed, it is advisable to ask the commune- or ward-level People's Committee or the Department of Construction where the apartment building is located which authority now receives such requests.
